interest: Shows Cuban geographer Massip's 1940 lecture tour in Japan, tracked by US diplomats, amid garbled press coverage of his name.
overview: This file comprises State Department diplomatic correspondence, telegrams, despatches, and newspaper enclosures from June to September 1940 regarding the visit of Cuban geographer and former diplomat Dr. Salvador Massip to Japan. Triggered by a report from U.S. Ambassador George S. Messersmith in Havana noting Massip's departure for Japan on an undefined lecture mission, Secretary of State Cordell Hull instructed Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo to monitor and report on Massip's activities. Grew transmitted Despatch No. 4887 with an enclosed interview from The Japan Times of July 19, 1940, revealing that Massip and his wife were on a five-month academic tour to foster Cuban-Japanese cultural ties, promote student and professor exchanges, and connect with Japanese academic and official figures, after which Grew's findings were relayed back to the embassy in Havana.
